approved: owner 2026-10-30 (scored now: it could happen now; Aave v3 and Compound v3; industry-standard delay; bands as proposed)
question: If a treasury wallet's signing control were compromised, how much could leave within one hour as liquid assets nobody can freeze?
delay_standard_source: Compound Timelock MINIMUM_DELAY = 2 days (compound-finance/compound-protocol, contracts/Timelock.sol), the timelock Uniswap and many DAOs reuse
protected_when: every control path needs an on-chain vote or a delay of at least delay_standard_hours
unknown_control_path: counted as extractable and flagged, unless a cited curated control path says otherwise

paths.direct: liquid, non-freezable tokens the wallet can transfer now; lent positions only up to the share a signed exit check measured as withdrawable
paths.borrow: collateral escape: plain freezable tokens x the best collateral factor (Aave v3 LTV, Compound v3 borrow collateral factor); lent positions (freezable, or the part that cannot be withdrawn) x LTV up to the account's unused Aave v3 borrowing room; per chain capped by the WETH cash the Aave v3 core pool and the Compound v3 WETH market hold
paths.freezable: issuer-freezable stablecoins count only through the borrow path; the rest is reported as freezable
paths.locked: positions flagged lockup or unlock_pending, and locked_unverifiable assets, cannot leave within the hour

freezable_rule: the issuer's token contract can block an address (Circle, Tether, Paxos, First Digital, TrueUSD, Ripple, World Liberty Financial, Gemini); a lending receipt of one (e.g. aEthUSDC) counts as freezable
